originality.rationale: The present full, dimension-uniform pairwise nonnegative identity and sharp Gaussian versus signs spike exponent are not direct consequences of the examined prior low-rank bounds. The most relevant 2023 full text treats broad sub-Gaussian classes with unspecified constants, while the 2026 paper proves worst-case-over-matrices minimax rotation-invariance; neither implies a pointwise optimal iid coordinate-magnitude law on the prescribed right-singular alignment. An earlier two-dimensional q=0 special-case comparison was explicitly excluded from the novelty claim. Publication priority remains best-knowledge, not certified uniqueness.
residual_risks: More general results on exchangeable normalized weighted means or ratios may imply the pairwise sign extremality without referring to sketching.
The 2018 canonical-angle primary paper was not inspected in complete full text in this run; its unviewed details were not used as a negative coverage assertion.
No exhaustive literature uniqueness certification is possible; searched texts and indexed research records may omit specialized overlap.
The assumption of right-singular-coordinate alignment is essential and prevents an orientation-free claim.

value.rationale: One-vector spectral sketching is a natural simplest nontrivial regime of randomized low-rank approximation. The distribution-free iid magnitude comparison is global, not a perturbation or selected numerical case, and supplies a positive exact loss certificate for every nondegenerate amplitude law. The one-spike limit proves different q-dependent convergence exponents for two common equal-cost sketch choices, identifying a quantitatively important rare-small-leading-coordinate effect. This matters for method selection when a singular basis is available or approximately aligned, while the documented orientation limitation prevents overgeneralization.
